title: Cross-document Event Identity via Dense Annotation
research_question: How can cross-document event identity be densely annotated so that both full event identity and important forms of partial or quasi-identity are represented?
methodology: The authors construct related storylines from English Wikinews and automatically extract open-domain event mentions, followed by expert correction. Crowd workers then inspect pairs of documents and densely link event mentions across the pair, with follow-up questions about overlap in time, location, participants, and event inclusion. The resulting CDEC-WN corpus is analyzed for different kinds of partial identity, and two mention-pair baselines, including a neural cross-encoder, are evaluated on held-out subtopics. The study deliberately represents coreference as pairwise links rather than forcing all links into transitive event clusters.

key_findings.finding: CDEC-WN contains 7,220 event mentions and 4,282 cross-document event links across 198 document pairs drawn from 55 subtopics.
About 32 percent of the annotated cross-document links were identified as candidates for partial rather than full event identity.
The analysis identifies membership, subevent relations, and a newly proposed spatiotemporal-continuity category as important forms of quasi-identity.
Partial event identity can violate transitivity, making conventional event clustering an imperfect representation for these links.
The neural cross-encoder reaches 57.6 test F1 compared with 48.2 for the lemma-matching baseline, but performance remains limited, particularly on partial identity.
The corpus contains substantially denser event annotation per document than several earlier cross-document event-coreference resources.

limitations: The corpus is limited to English Wikinews.
The released study focuses on the Disasters and Accidents domain.
The annotation covers cross-document relations but does not add within-document event coreference.
The authors acknowledge that some coreference links may be missing or incorrect despite quality-control procedures.
The baseline evaluation assumes gold event mentions and known subtopics.
The pairwise representation accommodates non-transitive quasi-identity but does not directly produce globally coherent event clusters.
raw_claims: CDEC-WN was built from English Wikinews articles grouped into related storylines.
The corpus contains 176 documents organized into 198 cross-document pairs.
Its 7,220 event mentions participate in 4,282 annotated cross-document links.
The annotations distinguish 2,914 full-coreference links from 1,368 partial-identity links.
Annotators record whether linked events overlap in participants, time, and location.
Membership and subevent relations are recurring forms of partial event identity.
Spatiotemporal continuity is proposed as another form of quasi-identity.
The authors avoid mandatory clustering because partial identity is not always transitive.
A cross-encoder outperforms a lemma-based baseline but still has difficulty with partial identity.
